round1_to_round2.dispersion: Fair values went from $260-293 (range $33, mean $274.4) to $255-265 (range $10, mean $260.6). Thesis breaks went from $205-215 to $205-212. The cross-agent range of P(close >= K) at K=294 fell from 0.055 to 0.015, and at K=235 from 0.049 to 0.024. The mean ladder moved down: P(>=294) went from 0.476 to 0.458, and the median from about $288 to about $283. The 1-month mean at spot went from 0.504 to 0.485, which is the ex-dividend shift.
round1_to_round2.independence_verdict: Round 2 converged for two reasons, and only the first is independent agreement. (1) Verified facts: the $10.10 LSEG consensus, Q2 EPS of $2.14, $2.16B of CHIPS receivables, the ex-dividend date of Oct 30, net debt of $7.1B before the deal, and the China AD termination commitment. Agents 1, 3, 4 and 5 re-read these themselves. Agent 2 says it took the TI filing figures from my file without re-opening them. Converging on corrected facts is legitimate. (2) Anchoring on my round-1 judgments. Every agent adopted my about-21x core median and landed its applied multiple inside my '15-20% justified premium' band (23.5-25x). Four agents used my '-$0.2 to -0.4' SLAB amortization figure, and agents 2, 3 and 5 cite it as 'the supervisor's estimate' without deriving it. Three thesis breaks were re-based to 'about 21x CY27', my formula. Agents 2 and 3 repeated my 'industry-high gross margin' premium argument. The clearest sign of anchoring is that three of my round-1 judgments turned out wrong this round and propagated through most of the files: GAAP amortization deducted from EPS that is then valued on peer adjusted multiples; TXN having the 'industry-high gross margin', when ADI's FQ3-26 GAAP gross margin is 67.3% (72.5% adjusted) against TI's ~61%; and the claim that Zacks is 'stale' against rising LSEG revisions, when Yahoo's own trend table shows CY27 flat at $10.10 for 30 days. The ladders are the exception. Agents built their distributions themselves, and all of them landed below my round-1 ladder (medians $281-285 vs my $288), so the 12-month ladders are not copies. Truly independent new inputs this round, all verified: agent 5's base rates, agent 4's ECIA and Avnet data, agent 2's WSTS forecast and 2010/2018 precedents, and agent 3's 2026 sell-side record. Net: about two-thirds of the fair-value convergence is anchoring on supervisor judgment, not independent agreement. The cross-agent spread understates the true uncertainty and should not be read as extra confidence.

disagreements.topic: Premium justification: does TXN have the 'industry-high gross margin'?
disagreements.positions: Agents 2 and 3, and my round-1 comps_review, cite 'highest gross margin in the set (61%)' as the main persistent reason for a premium. Agent 4 notes ADI is at about 70%.
disagreements.resolution: Wrong. ADI's fiscal Q3-26 GAAP gross margin was 67.3% (adjusted 72.5%) on +40% y/y revenue, against TI's ~61% on +23%. TXN trades at 29.1x CY27 against ADI's 25.0x, even though ADI has higher margins and faster growth. So the margin leg of the premium argument falls away. What remains persistent is that TXN's FCF exceeds net income through 2028 (depreciation above falling capex), its 300mm capacity is owned so it can supply through a shortage, it returns about 100% of FCF, and it has low leverage. These support a 5-15% premium to the core median and a ceiling below ADI. I reconcile to 23x (+11%). Agents 1, 3 and 4 at 23.5-24x are at the upper edge. Agent 5 at 25x (ADI parity) is not supported.
disagreements.evidence: ADI 8-K Ex.99.1, 2026-08-19 (FQ3-26: revenue $4,022M +40%; GM 67.3% GAAP / 72.5% adjusted; GAAP EPS $2.74 vs adjusted $3.45); TI Q2-26 release

disagreements.topic: Agent 5's GAAP-vs-adjusted EPS argument for a 21% premium (25x)
disagreements.positions: Agent 5 says peers' consensus EPS is adjusted (ex amortization) while TXN's is GAAP, so on a 'like-for-like GAAP basis' the peer median is about 24-26x and 25x on TXN is not really a premium.
disagreements.resolution: Rejected. TXN has negligible acquisition amortization, so its GAAP EPS is already close to an amortization-adjusted EPS. Comparing it with peers' adjusted EPS is like-for-like on amortization. Restating peers on GAAP charges them for a non-cash item TXN does not have, which makes the comparison less like-for-like, not more. Only stock-based compensation (excluded by some peers, e.g. MCHP and NXPI, but included in TI's GAAP) is a real basis gap, worth about 3-5% on some names. So the argument supports at most about 3-5%, and agent 5's P/E multiple should fall to about 23-24x (about -$10-15 on its P/E leg).
disagreements.evidence: Agent 5's own ratios (ADI GAAP/adjusted 0.75; MCHP 0.32) are driven by Maxim/Microsemi purchase amortization; ADI FQ3-26 release reconciliation

disagreements.topic: SLAB purchase amortization deducted from EPS while applying peer adjusted multiples
disagreements.positions: Agents 1 (-$0.36 amortization, -$0.28 net), 3 (-$0.25), 4 (-$0.25) and 5 (-$0.25) deduct GAAP purchase amortization from horizon EPS. Agent 2 excludes it 'to match peers' adjusted EPS'. My round-1 file asked agent 1 to add it.
disagreements.resolution: Agent 2 is right, and my round-1 instruction was a basis error. A peer-median multiple built on adjusted EPS (amortization excluded) must be applied to TXN EPS before purchase amortization. On that basis the deal is about EPS-neutral: about -$0.31 of financing and lost interest against SLAB 2028E NOPAT of $260M (about $0.28; verified in the proxy, a non-GAAP figure that excludes SBC) plus early synergies. Removing the deduction adds about $6-8 to the P/E legs of agents 1, 3, 4 and 5 (about $4-5 to their blended fair values). GAAP dilution still matters for headline EPS optics after close.
disagreements.evidence: SLAB DEFM14A (Company Projections: NOPAT 2027E $168M, 2028E $260M; non-GAAP EPS excludes SBC and amortization); TI 8-K 2026-02-04 (accretive excluding transaction-related costs)

disagreements.topic: Estimate momentum: is CY27 consensus still being revised up?
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 3, 4 and 5 justify a 12-month median $20-30 above fair value partly by '22-24 upward revisions and none down in 30 days'. I made the same claim in round 1 and used it to call Zacks stale.
disagreements.resolution: Partly wrong. Yahoo's EPS Trend table shows the CY27 consensus at $10.10 now, $10.10 7 days ago and $10.10 30 days ago. It was $10.03 60 days ago and $8.89 90 days ago. The upgrade cycle came after the July report and has stalled for a month; the 'up revisions' counts sit beside an unchanged level and are not reliable. Zacks showing no change in 4 weeks is consistent with this. The $9.84 vs $10.10 gap is a difference in panel size, not staleness. The broader $10.10 figure stays as the base. Meanwhile the price has already fallen from $332 (Jun 22) to $294 while CY27 estimates rose about 13%, so de-rating is under way. Momentum is a weaker reason to hold the median above fair value than agents claimed. That is the main reason I shade the ladder about 1% lower.
disagreements.evidence: finance.yahoo.com/quote/TXN/analysis (EPS Trend: 10.1/10.1/10.1/10.03/8.89; fetched 2026-10-04); api.nasdaq.com TXN earnings-forecast (Zacks CY27 $9.84, 13 estimates)

disagreements.topic: Scenario mean, ladder and fair value are not reconciled within each agent
disagreements.positions: Fair value / probability-weighted scenario mean / ladder median / approximate ladder mean: agent 1 $264 / $290 / $283 / ~$300; agent 2 $257 / $285 / $282 / ~$297; agent 3 $255 / $285 / $284 / ~$300; agent 4 $265 / $288 / $281 / ~$296; agent 5 $262 / $285 / $285 / ~$298.
disagreements.resolution: In every file the scenario mean is 8.6-11.8% above fair value, and the ladder mean (lognormal skew at 32-37% sigma) is a further ~$10-15 above the scenario mean, about 2% above spot. Only agent 1 notes the scenario-vs-ladder gap, and none reconciles either number to fair value. A consistent reading exists: fair value is today's intrinsic value. If it compounds at about 9% cost of equity less a 2% yield, full convergence gives about $275-280 in a year and no convergence about $314. A ladder mean of about $300 then assumes about 40-50% of the 11% overvaluation closes in 12 months. The 3-point scenario sets imply 70-90% closure because they truncate the tails. No agent cites a base rate for convergence speed. The only empirical anchor is agent 5's base rate (post-2003, after >45% trailing gains: median -1%, 47% positive, n=38 overlapping months), which is consistent with a ladder median a little below spot. I keep the ~40-50% convergence implied by the ladders, but agents should state it and make their scenario sets match their ladders.
disagreements.evidence: Own arithmetic on the agent files; agent 5's base rates reproduced from Yahoo monthly adjusted closes 1990-2025 (n=93, median +12.4%, 57% positive; post-2003 n=38, median -1.1%, 47% positive)

disagreements.topic: Net debt at the horizon (agent 2's EV/EBITDA leg)
disagreements.positions: Agent 2: about $9.0B at Oct-2027 (its own build, using MarketScreener FCF of $8.2B/$9.8B less dividends, less a further $1.0B of CHIPS). Agent 5: $12.3B at SLAB close (no roll-forward).
disagreements.resolution: Rolling forward 5 quarters (Q3-26 to Q3-27): CFO about $12.3B, less capex of about $2.8B, plus about $1.2B of CHIPS collections (TI's FCF definition already includes CHIPS), less dividends of $1.52 x 912M x 5 = $6.9B, retains about $3.8B. $7.15B + about $7.5B SLAB outlay incl. costs - $3.8B gives about $10.8B at Oct-2027. Agent 2's $9.0B double-counts CHIPS and uses an FCF feed above TI's run-rate, overstating its EV/EBITDA leg by about $2 a share (about $1 on its blend). Agent 5's $12.3B is right at close but about $1.5B high for an Oct-2027 valuation (about $1.6 a share on a 15% leg, negligible).
disagreements.evidence: TI 10-Q Q2-26 (debt $14,150M; cash+STI $7,001M; CHIPS receivable $1,005M + $1,158M); TI 8-K 2026-09-17 ($1.52 quarterly dividend)

disagreements.topic: Recurring FCF per share and the FCF-yield legs
disagreements.positions: Recurring FCF/share ex-CHIPS: agent 1 $9.76 (45% CFO margin, $2.0B capex), agent 3 $8.44 (2027E), agent 4 about $11.0 (CY28 EPS + D&A - capex, an implied CFO margin of about 50%), agent 5 $9.43. Yields 3.3-4.0%.
disagreements.resolution: Agent 4's $11.0 implies a CFO margin of about 50%, which TI reached only at the 2021 peak (about 48%), and assumes no haircut to CY28. About $10 (about $9.1B on 912M shares) is the reconciled mid-point. The yield should be consistent with the P/E leg: at 23x on about $10.8 of EPS, the implied FCF yield on $10 is about 4%. I use 3.75%, crediting FCF above net income while depreciation exceeds capex. The legs then bracket $248 (P/E) and $268 (FCF incl. CHIPS).
disagreements.evidence: TI Q2-26 release (TTM CFO $8,667M, capex $3,312M, CHIPS $1,179M); TI 10-K history (2021 CFO $8.76B on $18.3B revenue)

one_month_reasoning: I keep the round-2 forecaster mean, which already shifts the centre down by the $1.52 dividend (ex Oct 30, the last close before the Sunday Nov 1 horizon) and spans the Q3 report expected Wed Oct 21 after the close. TI had still not confirmed that date by Oct 4, and I found no webcast notice. Q3 consensus is $2.42 against a $2.40 guide midpoint and Q4 is $2.28, both flat for 30 days. Three things keep the print two-sided: the stock rose 4.4% on Oct 2 with the sector, ECIA distributor sentiment peaked in June (154.1 to 136.7 in August), and the last six earnings-day moves averaged about 9%. The China AD probe is not a window event.
confidence_reason: This round's searches settled real factual points: ADI's higher gross margin, a flat 30-day consensus, the amortization basis, agent 5's premium logic, and net debt. These move fair value by only about -2% against the forecaster mean, and they partly offset (removing the amortization deduction adds about $5; a lower justified multiple takes away about $8). The ladder change is a 1% shift in the centre. Nothing settled here clearly beats the mean.
thesis_break_reason: $210 is about 20.7x the $10.10 CY27 consensus, which is the core analog peer median with no premium at all, and about 19.5x horizon NTM EPS. Reaching it within 12 months in a normal market would most likely mean the 2026 shortage has turned into a destocking or double-ordering correction: lead times and broker premiums collapse, distributor book-to-bill falls below 1, ECIA sentiment heads toward 100, and Q1/Q2-27 guides come in below seasonal. Other routes are China breaking the Nov-2025 truce with analog duties, or a 2027 recession (Kalshi about 19%). Agents' levels are $205-212; mine is unchanged from round 1.
key_drivers: Valuation: 29.1x CY27 LSEG consensus ($10.10; 29.9x on Zacks $9.84) against a 20.7x core analog/MCU median, a 41-44% premium, and above ADI (25.0x), which has higher margins (FQ3-26 GAAP GM 67.3% vs TI ~61%) and faster growth (+40% vs +23% y/y). A justified premium is about 5-15%, so the multiple likely keeps compressing even if numbers are met.

Cycle position: Q2-26 revenue +23% y/y against WSTS analog market growth of +10.2% in 2026 and +6.6% in 2027. TI is enforcing price increases on open POs and lead times are stretching (Fusion Greensheet), but ECIA sentiment has rolled over from its June peak and consensus CY27 EPS has been flat for 30 days. These are classic late-upcycle markers (2010, 2018 precedents).

FCF inflection: capex falls from $4.9B toward $2-3B while depreciation rises, and $2.16B of CHIPS incentives remain receivable. Recurring FCF is about $10 a share by 2028, and FCF exceeds net income through 2028. This is the one premium factor that clearly persists.

Silicon Labs: about $7.3B net outlay, closing H1-2027 (HSR expired May 22, 2026; other approvals pending). Net debt is about $12.3B at close and about $10.8B by Oct-2027 (about 1x EBITDA). About EPS-neutral before purchase amortization, which is non-GAAP-comparable with peers; GAAP dilution about $0.25-0.35.

Base rate: after >45% trailing 12-month gains, TXN's next-12-month median was +12% across 1990-2025 (57% positive, n=93 overlapping months) but -1% after 2003 (47% positive, n=38). This anchors a median near or slightly below spot.

fair_value.reason: P/E leg, 60%: horizon NTM EPS = 0.25 x CY27 $10.10 + 0.75 x CY28 $11.60 less 5% (thin 5-estimate panel, late cycle) = $10.79. SLAB is about neutral before purchase amortization (about -$0.31 financing against about $0.28 of 2028E NOPAT less SBC plus early synergies), so about $10.78. At 23x, the 20.7x core median plus an 11% premium for FCF conversion, owned capacity and capital returns, capped below ADI's 25x because ADI has higher margins and growth, that is $248. FCF leg, 40%: recurring FCF of about $10.0 a share ($9.1B on 912M shares) at 3.75% is $267, plus about $1 of CHIPS receivable still uncollected at the horizon, for $268. The blend is about $256, 13% below spot. Versus the round-2 forecaster mean of $260.6: removing the GAAP amortization deduction adds about $5; the lower justified multiple (ADI margin fact, agent 5's invalid GAAP argument) and a consistent FCF yield subtract about $9. My round-1 figure of $270 used 24.5x and a 3.5% yield.

IFX (0.75 FY Sep-27 + 0.25 FY Sep-28), Renesas (FY Dec), Melexis (FY Dec) and ROHM (FY Mar, calendarized) use MarketScreener. All prices are 2026-10-02 closes. comps_review.justification: Persistent through Oct-2027, with evidence: FCF above net income while depreciation exceeds falling capex through 2028, plus $2.16B of CHIPS receivables (10-Q); owned 300mm capacity that lets TI supply and enforce price in a shortage (Fusion Greensheet); a policy of returning about 100% of FCF, with the dividend raised 7% in Sep-26; leverage about 1x EBITDA after SLAB. Not persistent or not true: the 'industry-high gross margin' (ADI is 67.3% GAAP vs TI ~61%) and agent 5's GAAP-basis argument (TXN GAAP EPS is already amortization-free). Against any premium: TXN's CY27 growth (+19%) is the lowest of the core peers except Renesas, its cyclicality matches peers (2022-24 revenue down about 30%), and its multiple compressed late in the 2018 and 2022 upcycles. So the defensible range is 5-15% over 20.7x (21.7-23.8x), and the multiple should not reach ADI's 25x. Agent verdicts: agents 1 and 4 (23.5x, +13.5%) are at the upper edge and acceptable. Agents 2 and 3 (24x, +16%) are slightly above the band, and their argument relies on the wrong gross-margin claim. Agent 5 (25x, +21%) is unjustified: the GAAP argument fails, so this is a correction to send back. Sell-side calls were not used.

summary: Round 2 corrected the facts but anchored on my round-1 judgments. Fair values collapsed to $255-265 and applied multiples to 23.5-25x, and two of my round-1 claims turned out wrong and spread through the files: TXN does not have the industry-high gross margin (ADI is at 67.3%), and CY27 consensus has been flat at $10.10 for 30 days, not rising. I reconcile fair value to about $256 and keep the forecasters' ladder, shaded about 1% lower (median about $280).
